definition: The 1.7B Qwen3 base checkpoint, used across 7 sources as the small end of the ladder in on-policy distillation and group-relative training studies. It is where the archive's most carefully controlled distillation comparisons run -- three-seed paired evaluations with bootstrap intervals stratified by problem and seed, rollout-matched and equal-FLOP baselines -- because it is small enough to train repeatedly. Two measured results: it is one of the models where fine-tuning on 800 heavily hedged traces degrades rather than improves performance, against three models it improves by up to 2.6-fold, and it is a strong-mismatch student in one distillation study, starting at 6.9 percent and emitting 22K-token unterminated responses under the standard objective. As with the other small checkpoints, its competition-benchmark scores are low enough that a multi-benchmark average is carried by the easier sets.

evidence.note: Inserts a stage before RL in which the model extracts textual lessons from its own successful and failed rollouts, filters them by measured marginal utility on a held-out probe set, and distills the surviving pool into its own weights — so that GRPO starts from a policy that fails all-eight-samples less often.
evidence.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

evidence.note: Treats a policy's per-problem failure probability as a random variable over the problem distribution and shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimize a single moment of it, then proposes minimizing the first T moments jointly — which is exactly minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to reach a first success.
evidence.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
evidence.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

evidence.note: Gives the teacher branch of an on-policy self-distillation setup an abstract skill card -- a principle, when it applies, and the mistakes to avoid -- instead of the reference solution, so the privileged signal carries no answer and the gain lands on exactly the rollout groups where group-relative reward is algebraically silent.
evidence.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Evaluates on-policy distillation across sampling budgets from 1 to 1024 and finds it consistently improves accuracy at small budgets while losing to the untrained base model at large ones, so what it transfers is sampling efficiency rather than capability -- and off-policy distillation, tested the same way, does expand the boundary.
evidence.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Separates reasoning into procedural advancement and 'epistemic verbalization' — the token-level externalization of uncertainty — and shows that emitting doubt is what lets a model recover from silent divergence, that injecting a bare doubt cue recovers failed trajectories, and that 800 SFT examples suffice to install or destroy the habit.
evidence.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

name: Qwen3-1.7B-Base
